faq.q: What types of industrial safety signs are available?
faq.a: The range covers Warning signs, Danger signs, Caution signs, Prohibition signs, Mandatory signs, PPE safety signs, Fire Safety signs, Emergency Exit signs, Equipment Safety signs and Warehouse Safety signs. Signs are produced to order, so types can be mixed freely within one order — for example a full facility set of machinery warnings, PPE requirements, fire equipment markers and warehouse traffic signs in matching materials and finishes. If you have a hazard list or an existing sign schedule, it can be used directly as the basis for production.

faq.q: Can industrial safety signs be customized with company logos?
faq.a: Yes. Safety signs can carry your company logo, site name or other identification, placed so it does not interfere with the safety message itself. Wording, pictograms, colours and supplementary text — including multilingual text you supply — are set to your requirements. A proof of each sign type is prepared for your confirmation before production. Please note that it is the buyer's responsibility to confirm that the final sign designs meet the regulations applying at the installation site.

faq.q: Which materials are suitable for factory safety signs?
faq.a: Aluminum and other metals suit long-term and outdoor use: they are rigid, do not rust (in aluminum's case) and hold printed and reflective faces well. Rigid plastics are lighter and economical for indoor areas, and self-adhesive labels serve small equipment-level messages. The suitable material depends on the environment — indoor or outdoor, exposure to sun, moisture or chemicals, sign size, fixing method and expected life. State these conditions in your enquiry and the material and thickness will be confirmed in the quotation rather than assumed from the sign type alone.

faq.q: Are reflective industrial safety signs available?
faq.a: Yes, reflective face options are available alongside non-reflective ones. Reflective signs are most useful where signs are read by vehicle drivers — forklift routes, loading docks, yard crossings and gate areas — and for fire and emergency signs in areas that may lose lighting. Indoor signs under constant lighting usually do not need a reflective face. Reflective films are supplied in different grades; the film type and grade for your order are confirmed in the quotation, and any specific performance requirement should be stated in your enquiry so it can be checked explicitly.

faq.q: Can safety signs be manufactured in different sizes and colors?
faq.a: Yes. Signs are made to the sizes your viewing distances and mounting positions require, from small equipment labels to large facility boards, and colours follow the designs you supply or approve — including your existing site colour scheme. Where a sign design is governed by rules at your site, supply the required design or reference and it will be reproduced as specified. Sizes, colours and quantities per type are listed in your sign schedule and confirmed in the quotation.

faq.q: Can you produce signs according to customer-provided designs?
faq.a: Yes — this is the normal way of working. Send print-ready artwork, design files, or photographs and dimensions of existing signs to be matched, and the signs are produced to those designs. If you have wording and symbol requirements but no finished artwork, the signs can be set up from your brief; proofs are returned for your confirmation before production in all cases. Basic file checks and minor adjustments are included; extensive design work is quoted separately before it begins.

faq.q: What information should I provide when ordering industrial safety signs?
faq.a: Please share: the sign types and exact wording required; the symbols, pictograms or reference designs to follow; finished sizes and quantities per type; preferred material and reflective or non-reflective face; mounting method (holes, adhesive, frames); and the delivery destination. A site sign schedule or hazard list, if you have one, is the most efficient starting point. Specifications, production and dispatch timing and pricing are then confirmed in the quotation for your order — no list prices or standard lead times are published.

faq.q: How do I choose the right industrial safety sign material?
faq.a: Start from the environment, not the sign. Ask: will it be indoors or outdoors? Will it face sun, rain, wash-down or chemicals? How large is it, and how will it be fixed? How long must it last? Outdoor, long-life and vehicle-read signs generally point to metal with a suitable face finish; indoor, short-life or frequently changed signs can often use rigid plastic. If you describe the conditions in your enquiry, we will confirm a material and thickness against them in the quotation and explain the reasoning, rather than simply quoting the cheapest construction.
